text:
sana: Heads-up — starting an experiment to change sequence-length gating. Goal: prefer decode-only path for very short contexts on H100, keep prefill-heavy path for long contexts, and add a small hysteresis window to avoid flip-flopping when KV usage is spiky.

matt: nice. can you share the perf numbers that motivated this?

sana: quick snapshot from yesterday's microbench on h100/xpu: 
```
arch: H100
context: 16 tokens
batch: 16
path: prefill+decode -> p50 8.2ms, p99 23.1ms
path: decode-only    -> p50 4.6ms, p99 12.8ms
kv-lookup overhead ~0.8ms

arch: A100
context: 16 tokens
path: prefill+decode -> p50 5.1ms, p99 15.4ms
path: decode-only    -> p50 6.3ms, p99 18.9ms
```
so H100 benefits a lot from skipping prefill for <~32 tokens, A100 still prefers prefill because its fused-prefill kernels are cheaper.

jiwoo: where is the KV pressure in these runs? i.e., when does eviction spike?

sana: KV headroom measured separately: when average active seq length > 48 we see KV residency > 85% and occasional thrash causing p99 jumps. that's why i'm proposing a KV threshold check before we switch to decode-only.

omar: proposed gating rule?

sana: prototype rule: 
- if arch == H100 and seq_len <= 32 -> prefer decode-only
- if arch == A100 and seq_len <= 16 -> prefer prefill (keep current)
- if kv_residency > 0.8 -> force prefill for next N requests (hysteresis N=3)
- add kernel_switch_count telemetry and kv_eviction_count to decide thresholds

matt: can we make that auto-tuneable? like a soft rule: choose path that reduces estimated per-token cost + latency penalty. maybe use existing autotune service to learn per-queue thresholds.

jiwoo: yes — we already have per-arch profiles. suggestion: introduce an "arch_slen_profile" that maps slen bins -> preferred path with confidence. autotuner can update confidence and hysteresis on deploy.

sana: exact flags i've been experimenting with: 
```
--slen-gating=hybrid 
--slen-bins="[0,16,32,64,128]" 
--slen-hysteresis=3 
--kv-threshold=0.8 
--kernel-pick-mode=arch-aware
```

eva: i'm down to run a canary if we have the metrics to watch. what should we collect?

omar: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, kernel_switch_count, kv_eviction_count, batch_fill_rate, and model-quality delta on our eval set (to catch any hallucination/regression from path changes).

sana: added a short perf regression check: if model-quality delta > 0.5% rollback. also will tag requests that hit hysteresis so we can slice by that.

matt: timeline? canary on a small h100 pool first, then a mixed A100 pool to validate arch differences.

eva: i can schedule canary for tonight 02:00 UTC on h100-dedicated-1 (low-traffic window).

omar: i'll add telemetry hooks: kv_eviction_count and kernel_switch_count + per-path tokens/sec to the collector. expecting to see kernel_switch_count drop if hysteresis works.

jiwoo: small note — make sure batching heuristics still play nice. if decode-only wins for slen=16 but batch size collapses (because we're too strict), throughput could drop. consider a min_batch fill override: allow prefill if batch_fill_rate < 0.5.

sana: good catch. i'll add that as a secondary condition. updated flag: 
```
--min-batch-fill=0.5  # if batch density low, prefer prefill to improve throughput
```

matt: link the canary to INF ticket so infra + perf dashboards are tracked: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2345

infra-bot: Canary scheduled by eva for h100-dedicated-1 at 2006503600. Deployment window: 02:00-04:00 UTC.

eva: after canary i'll roll to a small A100 pool for comparison (metrics expected to disagree).

sana: thanks all — i'll push the canary config and a short playbook for rollback. will post results in this thread tomorrow. :rocket:
